extracted.intended_audience: applicants and regulatory affairs professionals preparing NDAs (including 505(b)(2) applications) for FDA review
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and content standards for New Drug Applications (NDAs), with particular detail for 505(b)(2) applications, describing required summary, technical sections, samples, case reports, patent certifications, and exclusivity information to permit FDA review and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive index requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain a comprehensive index by volume number and page number to the summary under paragraph (c), the technical sections under paragraph (d), and the supporting information under paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index should allow reviewers to locate the summary, technical sections, and supporting information by volume and page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary: level and content
rubrics_metrics.description: NDA must contain a summary in enough detail that the reader may gain a good general understanding of the data and information in the NDA, including an understanding of the quantitative aspects of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary should synthesize all aspects of the NDA into a well-structured, unified document written at approximately the level of detail and editorial standards of refereed scientific and medical journals; data should be presented in tables and graphics where possible. FDA may use or share the summary with advisory committee members and officials. Guidance under §10.90(b) is available for preparing the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary: labeling and annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary must contain the proposed text of the labeling, including any Medication Guide if applicable, with annotations to the information in the summary and technical sections that support inclusion of each statement in the labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prescription drugs, statements must explain reasons for omitting any section/subsection of the §201.57 labeling format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary: pharmacologic class and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary must identify the pharmacologic class of the drug and discuss the scientific rationale for the drug, its intended use, and the potential clinical benefits of the drug product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary: marketing history outside United States
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary must briefly describe the marketing history, if any, of the drug outside the United States, listing countries marketed, countries withdrawn for safety/effectiveness reasons, and countries with pending marketing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must cover marketing by the applicant and, if known, marketing history by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary: CMC, nonclinical, PK/bioavailability, microbiology, clinical data summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary must include summaries of the chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) section; nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology; human pharmacokinetics and bioavailability; microbiology (for anti-infectives); and clinical data including statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each summary should provide sufficient quantitative detail for understanding and may be used to prepare the Summary Basis of Approval for public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary: concluding benefit-risk discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary must include a concluding discussion presenting benefit and risk considerations related to the drug, including discussion of any proposed additional studies or postmarketing surveillance the applicant intends to conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical sections: overall sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain technical sections with data and information in sufficient detail to permit the agency to make a knowledgeable judgment about whether to approve the NDA or whether grounds exist under section 505(d) to refuse approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required technical sections are enumerated (CMC; nonclinical pharmacology/toxicology; human PK/bioavailability; microbiology; clinical data; statistical; pediatric use).

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: drug substance description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a full description of the drug substance including physical and chemical characteristics and stability; name and address of manufacturer; method of synthesis (or isolation) and purification; process controls used during manufacture and packaging; and specifications necessary to ensure identity, strength, quality, purity, and bioavailability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tests, analytical procedures, and acceptance criteria (e.g., stability, sterility, particle size, crystalline form). NDA may propose alternatives; reference to current USP/NF may satisfy relevant requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: drug product description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of all components used in manufacture of the drug product and a statement of composition; specifications for each component; name and address of each manufacturer; description of manufacturing and packaging procedures and in-process controls; and specifications necessary to ensure identity, strength, quality, potency, and bioavailability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tests/analytical procedures/acceptance criteria (e.g., sterility, dissolution rate, container closure) and stability data with proposed expiration dating. Alternatives may be proposed; USP/NF reference may satisfy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: batch records for bioavailability/stability batches
rubrics_metrics.description: For each batch used in bioavailability/bioequivalence studies or primary stability study, provide batch production record; specifications for each component and the drug product; names and addresses of sources of active and noncompendial inactive components and container/closure; names/addresses of contract facilities and identification of operations performed by each; and results of tests required by §§211.84(d) and 211.165.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: master production record or production process description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the proposed or actual master production record, including a description of equipment to be used for commercial manufacture, or a comparably detailed description of the production process for a representative batch.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: environmental impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain either a claim for categorical exclusion under §25.30 or §25.31 or an environmental assessment under §25.40 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: optional early submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may, at its option, submit a complete CMC section 90 to 120 days before anticipated submission of remainder of NDA; FDA will review such early submissions as resources permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC section: field copy certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must include a statement certifying that the field copy of the NDA has been provided to the applicant's home FDA district office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology: content and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide descriptions, with graphs and tables, of animal and in vitro studies including pharmacological actions relevant to proposed indication; studies defining pharmacologic properties or pertinent to adverse effects; toxicological studies relevant to clinical uses (acute/subacute/chronic toxicity, carcinogenicity, route-specific toxicities); reproduction and developmental studies as appropriate; absorption/distribution/metabolism/excretion in animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each nonclinical laboratory study subject to GLP under part 58, include a statement of compliance with part 58 or a brief statement of reason for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human pharmacokinetics and bioavailability: study descriptions and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe each bioavailability and pharmacokinetic human study performed by or on behalf of the applicant, including analytical procedures and statistical methods, and a statement for each study that it either was conducted in compliance with IRB regulations in part 56 (or was not subject under §§56.104/.105) and was conducted in compliance with informed consent regulations in part 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tests/analytical procedures/acceptance criteria to assure bioavailability are described in CMC, include rationale and supporting data here; include a summarizing discussion and analysis of PK, metabolism, and bioavailability/bioequivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microbiology section (anti-infective drugs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For anti-infective drugs, describe microbiology data: biochemical basis of drug's action on microbial physiology; antimicrobial spectra including in vitro preclinical study results showing concentrations needed for effective use; known mechanisms of resistance with epidemiologic prevalence data; and clinical microbiology laboratory procedures needed for effective use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: clinical pharmacology studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and analyze each clinical pharmacology study, including a brief comparison of human study results with animal pharmacology and toxicology data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: controlled clinical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and analyze each controlled clinical study pertinent to a proposed use, including the protocol and the statistical analyses used to evaluate the study; note if report is an interim analysis and provide projected completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include controlled studies that have been discontinued or are incomplete, along with protocol and a brief description of results and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: uncontrolled clinical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe each uncontrolled clinical study, provide a summary of the results, and briefly state why the study is classified as uncontrolled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: other relevant data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and analyze any other data or information relevant to evaluation of safety and effectiveness obtained from any source, foreign or domestic, including controlled/uncontrolled studies of other uses, commercial marketing experience, published and unpublished reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: integrated summary of effectiveness and subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an integrated summary of data demonstrating substantial evidence of effectiveness for claimed indications; present effectiveness data by gender, age, and racial subgroups and identify any dosing modifications needed for specific subgroups; present other subgroup data when appropriate (e.g., renal failure, disease severity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness data must support dosage and administration section of labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: integrated safety summary and update reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an integrated summary of all available information about safety, including pertinent animal data, demonstrated or potential adverse effects, clinically significant drug/drug interactions, and other safety considerations; safety data must be presented by gender, age, and racial subgroups and other subgroups when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under section 505(i), applicant must update pending NDA with new safety information (‘safety update reports’) including case report forms for each patient who died or did not complete a study because of an adverse event (unless waived). Reports must be submitted 4 months after initial submission, in a resubmission following a complete response letter, and at other times as requested. Applicants are encouraged to consult FDA about form/content before first report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: abuse potential and overdosage studies
rubrics_metrics.description: If drug has potential for abuse, include description and analysis of studies/information related to abuse including proposal for scheduling; include studies related to overdosage (information on dialysis, antidotes, or other treatments if known).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: integrated benefits and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an integrated summary of the benefits and risks of the drug, including a discussion of why the benefits exceed the risks under conditions stated in the labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: human-subject compliance statement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each clinical study involving human subjects, include a statement that it either was conducted in compliance with IRB regulations in part 56 (or was not subject under §§56.104/.105) and was conducted in compliance with informed consent regulations in part 50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: CRO transfer disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If sponsor transferred any obligations for conduct of a clinical study to a contract research organization (CRO), include the name and address of the CRO, identification of the clinical study, and a listing of the obligations transferred; if all obligations were transferred, a general statement may be submitted in lieu of listing specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical data: audits of original subject records
rubrics_metrics.description: If original subject records were audited or reviewed by the sponsor to verify accuracy of case reports, include a list identifying each clinical study so audited or reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical section: controlled study analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the documentation and supporting statistical analyses used in evaluating each controlled clinical study (copy of information submitted under clinical data controlled study requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical section: safety statistical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include documentation and supporting statistical analyses used in evaluating safety information (copy of information submitted under clinical data integrated safety summary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pediatric use section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a section describing investigation of the drug for use in pediatric populations, including an integrated summary of clinical pharmacology studies, controlled/uncontrolled clinical studies, or other data relevant to safety and effectiveness in pediatric populations for claimed indications, with references to full study descriptions and information required under §314.55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples upon FDA request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon FDA request, applicant must submit samples to places identified by FDA; FDA generally will ask for submission to two or more Agency laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically requested samples include four representative samples of drug product proposed for marketing, drug substance used in that product, and reference standards/blanks (each in quantity sufficient to perform three times each test described in NDA). Also submit samples of finished market package if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archival copy: analytical procedures and labeling copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Archival copy of the NDA must contain three copies of analytical procedures and related descriptive information (sample descriptions; proposed regulatory specifications; detailed analytic methods; supporting data for accuracy, specificity, precision, ruggedness; complete results of applicant's tests) and copies of the label and all labeling (4 copies draft labeling or 12 copies final printed labeling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report tabulations: content and deletions
rubrics_metrics.description: NDA must contain tabulations of data from each adequate and well-controlled study (Phase 2/3), tabulations from earliest clinical pharmacology studies (Phase 1), and tabulations of safety data from other clinical studies; applicant may delete tabulations agreed in advance with FDA as not pertinent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-NDA conference can be used to agree deletions; normally agreed-to deletions will not be requested during review except under unforeseen circumstances and by the reviewing division director per paragraph (f)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report forms: deaths and discontinuations
rubrics_metrics.description: NDA must contain copies of individual case report forms for each patient who died during a clinical study or who did not complete the study because of an adverse event (whether believed drug-related or not), including patients receiving reference drugs or placebo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may waive this requirement for specific studies if case report forms are unnecessary for proper review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report additional data and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit additional case report forms and tabulations needed for proper review as requested by the reviewing division director; failure to submit requested information within 30 days may cause FDA to view an eventual submission as a major amendment under §314.60 and extend review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If desired, applicant may request written verification of an oral request for additional data from the division director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and format flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are invited to meet with FDA before submitting an NDA to discuss presentation and format of supporting information; if FDA and applicant agree, applicant may submit tabulations and case report forms in an alternate form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant ordinarily is not required to resubmit information previously submitted but may incorporate information by reference; a reference must identify the file by name, reference number, volume, and page number in the agency's records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reference to information submitted by a person other than the applicant must include a written statement authorizing the reference signed by the person who submitted the original information.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translations and originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit an accurate and complete English translation of each part of the NDA not in English and must submit a copy of each original literature publication for which an English translation is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reference/use statements for 505(b) reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant submitting under section 505(b) obtains a 'right of reference or use' to an investigation relied upon, the NDA must include a written statement signed by the owner of the data that the applicant may rely on the investigation, and must provide FDA access to the underlying raw data that provide basis for the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to 505(b) reliance; statement must be signed by data owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain the patent information described under §314.53.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent certification contents (Paragraphs I–IV) for each relevant patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A 505(b)(2) application must include, for each patent that in the applicant's opinion claims the drug substance/product or an approved use, an appropriate patent certification or statement identifying the patent number and certifying one of: Paragraph I (patent info has not been submitted), Paragraph II (patent has expired), Paragraph III (date patent will expire), or Paragraph IV (patent is invalid, unenforceable, or will not be infringed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Paragraph IV certification must be in the specified form and be accompanied by a statement that applicant will comply with notice requirements under §314.52(a)–(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: No relevant patents certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If, to the best of the applicant's knowledge, there are no patents that claim the drug or drugs on which investigations relied in the 505(b)(2) application were conducted or that claim a use of such drugs, applicant must provide a certification to that effect in the prescribed form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-of-use patent statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitted information concerns a method-of-use patent and the labeling does not include an indication/condition of use covered by that patent, applicant must explain that the method-of-use patent does not claim the proposed indication; if labeling includes an indication claimed by such a patent, applicant must submit the applicable certification (Paragraph I–IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing agreement disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 505(b)(2) application is submitted for a drug or method claimed by a patent and the applicant has a licensing agreement with the patent owner, the applicant must submit a Paragraph IV certification as to that patent and a statement that the applicant has been granted a patent license; if patent owner consents to approval as of a specific date, submit written statement of licensing agreement and consent to approval as of that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely filing of patent information rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an NDA holder does not file required patent information within 30 days of issuance, an applicant who submitted a 505(b)(2) before that filing and had an appropriate certification need not submit a certification addressing the late-listed patent. Certain submissions/ amendments to NDA holder's patent descriptions may still be considered untimely unless submitted within 30 days of specific events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant files 505(b)(2) after NDA holder's untimely filing or the application lacked an appropriate certification at time of patent submission, the applicant must submit the appropriate certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputed patent information procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant disputes accuracy or relevance of patent information submitted to FDA, applicant may seek confirmation of correctness under procedures in §314.53(f); unless withdrawn, applicant must submit an appropriate certification or statement for each listed patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to patent certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent certification or statement may be amended at any time before approval of the 505(b)(2) application; an amended certification must be submitted as an amendment to the pending application; if applicant voluntarily makes a certification for an untimely filed patent, applicant may withdraw that certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an amendment is submitted to change the certification, the application will no longer be considered to contain the prior certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of certification after finding of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submitted a Paragraph IV certification and is sued for patent infringement, applicant must amend its certification if a court enters a final decision (no appeal possible), or signs/enters a settlement order or consent decree that includes a finding that the patent is infringed (unless the decision also finds the patent invalid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment must certify the patent expiration date or provide method-of-use statement if applicant amends application so it is no longer seeking approval for the claimed method of use. If a final decision finds patent invalid and infringed, amendment not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after request to remove patent from list
rubrics_metrics.description: If NDA holder requests removal of a patent/information and no ANDA applicant is eligible for 180-day exclusivity based on a Paragraph IV to that patent, the patent/info will be removed and any applicant with pending 505(b)(2) who made a certification must submit an amendment to withdraw its certification, stating reason for withdrawal (patent removed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If removal would leave no patents listed for the listed drug(s), the applicant must submit an amended certification reflecting that no listed patents remain. If removal is for purposes of first applicant's 180-day exclusivity, patent may remain listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other certification amendment obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided elsewhere, applicant must amend a submitted certification if, before approval, the applicant learns the certification is no longer accurate; applicant must submit an appropriate certification if a new patent is issued after submission that, to applicant's best knowledge, claims a listed drug relied upon or claims an approved use for such drug and requires filing under section 505(b)/(c) and §314.53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is not required to submit a supplement to change a submitted certification for patent information submitted after approval of the 505(b)(2) application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimed exclusivity: statement and references
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant believes its new drug product is entitled to marketing exclusivity under §314.108, it must submit with the NDA prior to approval: a statement claiming exclusivity and a reference to the appropriate paragraph under §314.108 supporting the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimed exclusivity: information for §314.108(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If claiming exclusivity under §314.108(b)(2), submit information showing to the best of applicant's knowledge or belief that a drug with the same active moiety has not previously been approved under section 505(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimed exclusivity: information for §314.108(b)(4)/(b)(5) — new clinical investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: If claiming exclusivity under §314.108(b)(4) or (b)(5), provide information to show the NDA contains 'new clinical investigations' that are 'essential to approval' and were 'conducted or sponsored by the applicant', including a certification that each clinical investigation meets the definition of 'new clinical investigation' under §314.108(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide a list of all published studies/public reports known to applicant relevant to conditions for approval, certify thorough literature search and explain why published studies are insufficient without reference to new investigations; if applicant was sponsor named in Form FDA 1571 for an IND under which investigations were conducted, identify the IND by number.
